question: If f(x) = 2⁴ˣ ln(5x-4), then f prime(1) =
explanation:

explanation:

question: The cubic equation 4x³-6x²+9x+5=0

has only one real root in the interval (0,1)

subject: Maths
question: A cone has vertical angle 60°, and its total surface area increases at the rate of 10√3 cm²/sec. The rate of change of its volume when the radius is 10 cm is
explanation:

subject: Maths
question: The surface area of a sphere is 196 π sq cm. If it increases by 0.05 sq cm, the approximate increase in its volume (in cc) is
explanation:

dV/dS = ʳ⁄₂ = 3.5

subject: Maths
question: If the normal to the curve y²=12x at the point (12,12) meets the x-axis at A and the y-axis at B, then OA+OB (O is the origin) is
explanation:

question: The integral of dx/(x √(x²-25)) equals
explanation:

explanation:

explanation:

explanation:

question: The integral of (e⁶ˣ-1)/(e⁶ˣ+1) dx equals
explanation:

question: lim n tends to ∞ of the Σᵣ=₁ⁿ of r/n² equals

question: The value of the integral from π/6 to π/4 of sin2x/(1+cos2x) dx is
explanation:

subject: Maths
question: The value of the integral from -π to π of x⁵ cosx dx is
explanation:
The integrand x⁵ cosx is the product of an odd function (x⁵) and an even function (cosx), making the whole function odd
The integral of an odd function over the symmetric interval [-π,π] is 0

subject: Maths
question: The area of the region (in square units) bounded by the curve y=x²-36, the x-axis, and the lines x=-6, x=7 is
explanation:
The curve crosses the x-axis at x=-6 and x=6
Between x=-6 and x=6, the curve lies below the axis, contributing an area of 288 (absolute value)
Between x=6 and x=7, the curve lies above the axis, contributing an area of ¹⁹⁄₃

subject: Maths
question: If A and B are arbitrary constants, the differential equation for the family y=A e⁵ˣ+B e⁻⁵ˣ is
explanation:
y prime = 5A e⁵ˣ - 5B e⁻⁵ˣ
y double-prime = 25A e⁵ˣ + 25B e⁻⁵ˣ = 25y

subject: Maths
question: The general solution of the differential equation dy/dx = (4x²+y²)/(2xy) is
explanation:
This is a homogeneous equation, so substitute y=vx
After substitution, the equation reduces to 2v/(4-v²) dv = ᵈˣ⁄ₓ
Integrating gives -ln|4-v²| = ln|x| + C, which simplifies to x(4-v²) = constant
Substituting back v=ʸ⁄ₓ and simplifying gives 4x²-y² = Cx

subject: Maths
question: The general solution of the differential equation (4x+y-9)dy = (x+4y-6)dx is
explanation:
Shift variables using x=X+2, y=Y+1 to remove the constants, giving the homogeneous equation dY/dX=(X+4Y)/(4X+Y)
Substituting Y=vX and using partial fractions leads to (1+v)³/[(1-v)⁵ X²] = constant
Substituting back v=Y⁄X and simplifying gives (X+Y)³ = C(X-Y)⁵
Finally substituting X=x-2, Y=y-1 gives (x+y-3)³ = C(x-y+1)⁵

subject: Physics
question: If F, v, and t represent force, velocity, and time respectively, the quantity Fv has the dimensions of
explanation:
For a constant force F acting on an object moving with velocity v, the rate of doing work is P=Fv
So the quantity Fv has the dimensions of power

subject: Physics
question: A body falls freely under gravity from rest. The total displacement during the 3rd, 5th, and 7th seconds of its motion is (g=10 m/s²)
explanation:
Displacement in the nth second is given by 10n-5
3rd second: 10(3)-5=25 m
5th second: 10(5)-5=45 m
7th second: 10(7)-5=65 m
Total = 25+45+65 = 135 m

subject: Physics
question: The minimum velocity of a projectile during its motion is 15 m/s, and the ratio of its vertical to horizontal displacement at t=1s is 1:1. The angle of projection is (g=10 m/s²)
explanation:
The minimum speed occurs at the top of the trajectory and equals the horizontal component, so ux=15 m/s
Horizontal displacement at t=1: x=15(1)=15 m
Since the ratio is 1:1, vertical displacement y=15 m
y=uy(1)-(½)(10)(1)=uy-5=15, so uy=20 m/s
tan(θ)=ᵘʸ⁄ᵤₓ=²⁰⁄₁₅=⁴⁄₃, giving θ=tan⁻¹(⁴⁄₃)

subject: Physics
question: A body is projected at 80 m/s at 45° above the horizontal. The time taken for the velocity vector to become perpendicular to the initial velocity vector is (g=10 m/s²)
explanation:
Using the standard result, the time for the velocity to become perpendicular to the initial velocity is t=u/(g sin(θ))
With u=80, θ=45°, g=10: t=80/(10 x (√2/2))=80/(5√2)=8√2 s

subject: Physics
question: A small bead is placed on a circular loop of radius 20 cm rotating about its vertical diameter with angular velocity 15 rad/s. The angle made by the radius vector to the bead with the vertical downward direction is (g=10 m/s², neglect friction)
explanation:
For a bead on a rotating vertical circular wire, cos(θ) = g/(ω² r)
g=10, ω=15, r=0.2 m
ω² r = 225(0.2) = 45
cos(θ) = ¹⁰⁄₄₅ = ²⁄₉
θ = cos⁻¹(²⁄₉)

subject: Physics
question: A body placed at the top of an inclined plane of angle tan⁻¹(⁷⁄₂₄) takes time T to reach the bottom when smooth, and time 2T when rough. The coefficient of kinetic friction is
explanation:
On the smooth incline, a1=g sin(θ); on the rough incline, a2=g[sin(θ)-μ cos(θ)]
Since time doubles, a1=4a2
sin(θ) = 4[sin(θ)-μ cos(θ)]
4 μ cos(θ) = 3 sin(θ)
μ = (¾) tan(θ) = (¾)(⁷⁄₂₄) = ²¹⁄₉₆ = ⁷⁄₃₂

subject: Physics
question: A 12 kg block is pushed by a force of 250 N over a distance of 15 m on a surface with coefficient of friction 0.2. The final kinetic energy of the block is (g=10 m/s²)
explanation:
Friction force = 0.2 x 12 x 10 = 24 N
Net force = 250-24 = 226 N
Work done by the net force = 226 x 15 = 3390 J, which equals the final kinetic energy

subject: Physics
question: A force F=6x² is applied to move an object from x=0 to x=5 m. The work done is
explanation:
Work done = the integral of F dx from 0 to 5
= the integral of 6x² dx from 0 to 5
= 2x³ evaluated from 0 to 5
= 2(125) = 250 J

subject: Physics
question: A wire of mass m is bent into a semicircle of radius R. The moment of inertia about an axis through the center of the semicircle (the center of the original circle) perpendicular to its plane is
explanation:
For an axis perpendicular to the plane through the geometric center, every point of the semicircular wire is at the same distance R from the axis, regardless of the wire only spanning half the circle
So the moment of inertia is simply mR², the same as it would be for a full circular ring of the same mass and radius

subject: Physics
question: A ball moves in a horizontal circle with initial speed v0 and decelerates due to friction until it stops. The total work done by friction equals
explanation:
By the work-energy theorem, the total work done by friction equals the change in kinetic energy
Since the ball starts with kinetic energy (½)mv0² and ends at rest, the work done by friction equals (½)mv0² (with a negative sign indicating it removes this energy)

subject: Physics
question: A particle executes simple harmonic motion with time period T and amplitude A, starting from rest at the extreme position. The distance travelled in time ᵀ⁄₅ is
explanation:
Since the particle moves monotonically from the extreme position over this time (less than ᵀ⁄₄... actually ᵀ⁄₅ is less than ᵀ⁄₄), the distance equals A minus the displacement
x(t)=A cos(ω t), and at t=ᵀ⁄₅, ω t=2π/5=72°, giving x=A cos72=A(√5-1)/4
Distance travelled = A - A(√5-1)/4 = A[4-(√5-1)]/4 = A(5-√5)/4

subject: Physics
question: Two blocks of masses m and 6m connected by a spring of constant K are given velocities V in opposite directions towards each other. The maximum compression of the spring is
explanation:
The reduced mass is μ = m(6m)/(m+6m) = 6m/7
Relative velocity of approach = 2V
Kinetic energy in relative motion = (½)(6m/7)(2V)² = 12mV²/7
At maximum compression: (½)Kx² = 12mV²/7
x² = 24mV²/(7K)
x = V √(24m/(7K))

subject: Physics
question: The work required to shift an artificial satellite from an orbit of radius r to an orbit of radius 6r is
explanation:
Total energy in a circular orbit of radius r is E=-GMm/(2r)
Work done = E(6r)-E(r) = -GMm/(12r)-(-GMm/(2r)) = GMm[⁻¹⁄₁₂+½] = GMm(⁵⁄₁₂)/r = 5GMm/(12r)

subject: Physics
question: A material has a linear stress-strain graph with stress=140 N/m² at strain=7×10⁻³. The elastic energy density at a strain of 6×10⁻³ is
explanation:
Young modulus Y = ˢᵗʳᵉˢˢ⁄ₛₜᵣₐᵢₙ = 140/(7×10⁻³) = 2×10⁴ N/m²
At strain 6×10⁻³, stress = Y x strain = 2×10⁴ x 6×10⁻³ = 120 N/m²
Energy density = (½) x stress x strain = (½)(120)(6×10⁻³) = 0.36 J/m³

subject: Physics
question: A large tank is filled with water to height h and drains through a small hole at the bottom. The ratio of the time taken for the level to fall from h to ʰ⁄₆, to the time taken to fall from ʰ⁄₆ to zero, is
explanation:
Time to drain from h1 to h2 is ∝ √(h1)-√(h2)
Time for h to ʰ⁄₆ is ∝ √(h)-√(ʰ⁄₆) = √(h)[1-1/√6]
Time for ʰ⁄₆ to 0 is ∝ √(ʰ⁄₆) = √(h)/√6
Ratio = √6[1-1/√6] = √6-1

subject: Physics
question: The heat energy released when 7 kg of water is cooled by 22°Celsius is (specific heat of water = 4200 J/kg K)

subject: Physics
question: Three identical rods A, B, C meet at a common junction. The free end of A is at 0°Celsius, the free end of B is at 55°Celsius, and the free end of C is at 95°Celsius. The junction temperature is
explanation:
At steady state, heat flowing in from B and C equals heat flowing out through A
(55-T)/R + (95-T)/R = (T-0)/R
150-2T = T
150 = 3T
T = 50°C

subject: Physics
question: Two gases A and B start at the same pressure, volume, and temperature. A is compressed isothermally and B adiabatically, both to one-sixth the initial volume. The final pressure of A compared to B is
explanation:
Final pressure of A (isothermal): PA = ⁶P₀
Final pressure of B (adiabatic): PB = P0 . 6^γ, where γ is greater than 1
Since 6^γ is greater than 6, PB is greater than PA
So the final pressure of A is less than that of B

subject: Physics
question: Assertion (A): For an ideal gas undergoing free expansion into a vacuum, the temperature remains unchanged. Reason (R): In free expansion, no work is done and no heat is exchanged, so by the first law the internal energy stays constant, and for an ideal gas this means temperature stays constant since internal energy depends only on temperature.
options: Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, R is false
A is false, R is true
Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A
explanation:
In free expansion into a vacuum, the gas does no work against any external pressure (since it expands into empty space), and being an adiabatic process with no heat exchange, the internal energy remains unchanged
Since the internal energy of an ideal gas depends only on temperature, an unchanged internal energy means the temperature also remains unchanged
Both the assertion and reason are correct, and the reason correctly explains the assertion

subject: Physics
question: The temperature at which the rms speed of sulfur dioxide molecules equals the rms speed of neon molecules at 250 K is (M(SO2)=64, M(Ne)=20)
explanation:
v(rms) is ∝ √(ᵀ⁄M)
T(SO2)/M(SO2) = T(Ne)/M(Ne)
T(SO2) = 250 x (⁶⁴⁄₂₀) = 800 K

subject: Physics
question: A person at rest hears a stationary siren, then accelerates at 2.5 m/s². The distance travelled when the heard frequency drops to 94 percent of the initial value is (speed of sound=340 m/s)
explanation:
For an observer receding from a stationary source, f ᵖʳⁱᵐᵉ⁄f = (v-v0)/v
0.94 = (340-v0)/340
v0 = 340(0.06) = 20.4 m/s
Using v0²=2as: 20.4² = 2(2.5)s
416.16 = 5s
s is approximately 83.2 m

subject: Physics
question: An object is placed 36 cm from a convex lens of focal length 30 cm. A convex mirror is placed at the focus of the lens on the other side such that the final image coincides with the object. The focal length of the convex mirror is
explanation:
Using the lens formula with u=-36, f=30: ¹⁄ᵥ = ¹⁄₃₀-¹⁄₃₆ = ¹⁄₁₈₀, so v=180 cm
The mirror is placed at the focus, 30 cm from the lens, and the lens image would form at 180 cm from the lens, which is 150 cm from the mirror
For the final image to coincide with the object, this point must be the center of curvature of the mirror, so R=150 cm and the focal length is 75 cm

subject: Physics
question: For a prism of angle 8°, the minimum deviation versus refractive index graph is linear. The slope of the graph is
explanation:
For a thin prism, minimum deviation δ = (μ-1)A, which is linear in μ with slope A
Here A=8°, so the slope is 8°

subject: Physics
question: In Youngs double slit experiment, the ratio of maximum to minimum intensity is 64:1. The ratio of the intensities of the two slits is
explanation:
(root I1+root I2)/(root I1-root I2) = √(ᴵᵐᵃˣ⁄Iₘᵢₙ) = √64 = 8
Let r=√(ᴵ¹⁄I₂). Then (r+1)/(r-1)=8, giving r+1=8r-8, so r=⁹⁄₇
ᴵ¹⁄I₂ = r² = ⁸¹⁄₄₉

subject: Physics
question: Two point charges +7×10⁻¹⁹ C and -7×10⁻¹⁹ C are 2 Å apart, forming a dipole in a uniform field of 4×10⁵ V/m. The work done to rotate the dipole from equilibrium by 180° is
explanation:
Dipole moment p = qd = 7×10⁻¹⁹ x 2×10⁻¹⁰ = 1.4×10⁻²⁸ C.m
Work to rotate a dipole by 180° from stable equilibrium is W=2pE
W = 2 x 1.4×10⁻²⁸ x 4×10⁵ = 11.2×10⁻²³ J

subject: Physics
question: A circle of radius r is drawn in a uniform electric field E pointing left to right. J and K are the topmost and bottommost points on the diameter perpendicular to E, while L and M are the leftmost and rightmost points on the diameter along E. Then
explanation:
J and K lie on a line perpendicular to the field, so they are at the same potential, giving VJ=VK
Since potential decreases in the direction of the field, L (upstream, on the left) is at higher potential than M (downstream, on the right), giving VL greater than VM

subject: Physics
question: A 24 V battery is connected to two capacitors C1=6 microF and C2=12 microF in series, and this combination is in parallel with C3=10 microF. The charge on C1 is
explanation:
Series combination: Cs = (6×12)/(6+12) = ⁷²⁄₁₈ = 4 microF
This series branch is directly across the 24 V battery
Charge on the series combination = 4 x 24 = 96 microC
Since series capacitors carry the same charge, the charge on C1 is also 96 microC

subject: Physics
question: In a circuit, two 12 Ω resistors are in parallel, and this combination is in series with a third 12 Ω resistor, all connected to an 18 V source. The current drawn from the source is
explanation:
Parallel combination of the two 12 Ω resistors = 6 Ω
Total resistance = 6+12 = 18 Ω
Current = ⱽ⁄R = ¹⁸⁄₁₈ = 1 A

subject: Physics
question: In a circuit, two 9 Ω resistors are in parallel, and this combination is in series with a third 9 Ω resistor. Each resistor can dissipate a maximum power of 36 W. The maximum power the whole circuit can take is
explanation:
Parallel combination of two 9 Ω resistors = 4.5 Ω, in series with the third 9 Ω resistor gives total resistance 13.5 Ω
The series resistor is limiting, restricting current to at most √(³⁶⁄₉)=2 A
Maximum total power = I² x R(total) = 4 x 13.5 = 54 W

subject: Physics
question: Two parallel wires each carry current I and attract each other with a force per unit length F. If the current in each wire is doubled, the new force per unit length becomes
explanation:
The force per unit length between parallel currents is ∝ the product of the currents, F is ∝ I1.I2
Doubling both currents multiplies the product by 4, so the new force per unit length becomes 4F

subject: Physics
question: An electron in a circular orbit has angular momentum L=mvr. In terms of L, the elementary charge e, and mass m, its magnetic moment is
explanation:
The magnetic moment of an electron in a circular orbit is μ=ᵉᵛʳ⁄₂
Since L=mvr, we have vr=ᴸ⁄ₘ
Substituting gives μ = e(ᴸ⁄ₘ)/2 = eL/(2m)

subject: Physics
question: A material placed in a magnetic field shows a weak repulsion and tends to move from stronger to weaker regions of the field. This material is
explanation: Diamagnetic materials are weakly repelled by an external magnetic field and tend to move towards regions of weaker field strength, unlike paramagnetic and ferromagnetic materials which are attracted towards stronger field regions

subject: Physics
question: In a coil, the current varies from -5 A to +7 A in 6 s, inducing an emf of 0.6 V. The self-inductance of the coil is
explanation:
Change in current = 7-(-5) = 12 A over 6 s
emf = L(ΔI/Δt)
0.6 = L(¹²⁄₆) = 2L
L = 0.3 H

subject: Physics
question: For the power dissipated in an ᴸCR series circuit to be one twenty-fifth of the maximum power, the current amplitude should be
options: one twenty-fifth the maximum current amplitude
explanation:
Power dissipated is ∝ the square of the current amplitude
For power to be one twenty-fifth of the maximum, the current amplitude must be one-fifth of the maximum current amplitude

subject: Physics
question: Which of the following statements about electromagnetic waves are correct? (i) They are always transverse in nature (ii) They require a medium for propagation (iii) Their speed in vacuum is c=1/√(μ₀ ε₀) (iv) They do not carry momentum
explanation:
Electromagnetic waves are always transverse, so (i) is correct
They do not require a medium and travel through vacuum, so (ii) is incorrect
Their speed in vacuum is indeed given by c=1/√(μ₀ ε₀), so (iii) is correct
They do carry momentum, contrary to statement (iv), which is incorrect
Hence the correct statements are (i) and (iii)

subject: Physics
question: Light of wavelength 3000 Å is incident on a metal surface of work function 2.5 eV. The maximum kinetic energy of the photoelectrons is (approximately)
explanation:
Photon energy = 1240/(wavelength in nm) = ¹²⁴⁰⁄₃₀₀ = 4.13 eV
Maximum kinetic energy = photon energy - work function = 4.13-2.5 = 1.63 eV

subject: Physics
question: The energy of an electron in a Bohr hydrogen atom is -0.378 eV. The angular momentum of the electron is
explanation:
Energy -0.378 eV corresponds to n=6, since E(n)=-13.6/n² gives ⁻¹³.⁶⁄₃₆=-0.378 eV
Angular momentum L = nh/(2 π)

subject: Physics
question: The half-life of a radioisotope is 12 minutes. If the number of radioactive nuclei at a given instant is 5×10⁵, the number remaining 6 minutes later would be
explanation:
Since 6 minutes is half of the half-life (12 minutes), N = N0(½)ᵗ⁄ᵀ
N = 5×10⁵ x (½)⁶⁄₁₂ = 5×10⁵ x (½)⁰.5 = 5×10⁵/√2

subject: Physics
question: A carrier wave of frequency 6 MHz is used to modulate a message signal of frequency 60 kHz. The frequencies of the side bands produced are
explanation:
Side band frequencies are fc ± fm
fc = 6000 kHz, fm = 60 kHz
Side bands: 6000+60=6060 kHz and 6000-60=5940 kHz

subject: Physics
question: A uniform metre scale balances at the 35 cm mark when a mass of 40 g is suspended at the 26 cm mark. The mass of the scale is
explanation:
Since the scale is uniform, its weight acts at the 50 cm mark
Balancing torques about the 35 cm pivot: 40(35-26) = m(50-35)
40(9) = 15m
360 = 15m
m = 24 g

subject: Chemistry
question: A particle has mass 40 g and speed 250 m/s. If the speed is measured with an accuracy of 3 percent, the uncertainty in its position is (h=6.626×10⁻³⁴ J s, π=3.14)
explanation:
Uncertainty in velocity, Δv = 3 percent of 250 = 7.5 m/s
Using Δx is at least h/(4 π m Δv)
Δx = 6.626×10⁻³⁴/(4 x 3.14 x 0.04 x 7.5)
= 6.626×10⁻³⁴/3.768
= 1.76×10⁻³⁴ m

subject: Chemistry
question: The work functions of Ba, Cs, K, Ca are 2.5, 2.1, 2.3, 2.9 eV respectively. Light of wavelength 450 nm is shone on them. The metals that undergo the photoelectric effect are
explanation:
Photon energy = ¹²⁴⁰⁄₄₅₀ = 2.76 eV
Photoelectric effect occurs only when photon energy exceeds the work function
2.76 eV exceeds the work functions of Ba (2.5), Cs (2.1), and K (2.3), so all three undergo the effect
2.76 eV is less than the work function of Ca (2.9), so Ca does not

subject: Chemistry
question: Among B, C, N, O, the element with the highest first ionization enthalpy is
explanation:
Ionization enthalpy generally increases across a period, but nitrogen shows an anomalously high value due to its stable half-filled 2p3 configuration
This makes nitrogens first ionization enthalpy even higher than that of oxygen, giving it the highest value among these four elements

subject: Chemistry
question: The hybridization and shape of PCl₅ are respectively
explanation:
Phosphorus in PCl₅ has 5 bonding pairs and no lone pairs, giving 5 electron pairs total
This corresponds to sp3d hybridization
With all five positions occupied by bonding pairs, the resulting molecular shape is trigonal bipyramidal

subject: Chemistry
question: How many of the following are linear with no lone pair of electrons on the central atom: HgBr₂, CO₂, BeBr₂, SO₂, C₂H₂, N₂O?
explanation:
HgBr₂, CO₂, BeBr₂, C₂H₂, and N₂O are all linear species with no lone pair on the central atom in their principal structure
SO₂ is bent due to a lone pair on the central sulfur atom
So 5 of the molecules qualify

subject: Chemistry
question: At T(K), the rms velocity of an ideal gas is v m/s. At what temperature (in K) does the rms velocity become 7v m/s?
explanation:
v(rms) is ∝ √(T)
(7v/v)² = ᵀ²⁄T₁
49 = ᵀ²⁄T
T2 = 49T

subject: Chemistry
question: 12 g of a metal M reacts with chlorine to form 29.75 g of metal chloride. What is the mass of M that reacts with 40 g of oxygen?
explanation:
Mass of chlorine combined = 29.75-12 = 17.75 g
Equivalents of chlorine = ¹⁷.⁷⁵⁄₃₅.₅ = 0.5
Equivalent weight of M = ¹²⁄₀.₅ = 24
Equivalents of oxygen in 40 g = ⁴⁰⁄₈ = 5
Mass of M = 5 x 24 = 120 g

subject: Chemistry
question: Combustion of pentane gives CO₂(g) and H₂O(l). If the enthalpies of formation of C₅H₁₂(g), CO₂(g), H₂O(l) are -s, -t, -u kJ/mol respectively, the enthalpy of combustion of C₅H₁₂(g) is
explanation:
The combustion reaction is C₅H₁₂(g)+8O₂(g) to 5CO₂(g)+6H₂O(l)
Enthalpy of combustion = sum of enthalpies of formation of products minus that of reactants
= [5(-t)+6(-u)] - [(-s)+0]
= -5t-6u+s
= s-5t-6u

subject: Chemistry
question: Identify the correct statements: I. qv=ΔU at constant volume II. A bomb calorimeter operates at constant volume III. Extensive properties depend on the amount of substance present
explanation:
The relation qv=ΔU is a standard thermodynamic result for processes at constant volume, making I correct
A bomb calorimeter is a sealed, rigid vessel operating at constant volume, making II correct
Extensive properties, by definition, scale with the amount of substance present, making III correct

subject: Chemistry
question: Consider A(g)+B(g) reversible C(g)+D(g). In a 2 L closed flask, 4 moles of A and 2 moles of B are heated. At equilibrium, the concentration of C is twice the concentration of B. What is Kc?
explanation:
Let x moles react. At equilibrium: A=4-x, B=2-x, C=x, D=x
Given C=2B: x=2(2-x), so x=⁴⁄₃
Concentrations (dividing by 2 L): A=⁴⁄₃, B=⅓, C=⅔, D=⅔
Kc = (C)(D)/[(A)(B)] = (⅔ x ⅔)/(⁴⁄₃ x ⅓) = (⁴⁄₉)/(⁴⁄₉) = 1

subject: Chemistry
question: The dissociation constants of H₂A are Ka1=6×10⁻³ and Ka2=6×10⁻⁷. At equilibrium, [A2-]=[H₂A]. The approximate concentration of H⁺ at equilibrium is
explanation:
Multiplying the equilibrium expressions for Ka1 and Ka2 eliminates the intermediate species: Ka1 x Ka2 = [H⁺]² [A2-]/[H₂A]
Since [A2-]=[H₂A], this ratio is 1, so [H⁺]² = Ka1 x Ka2 = 36×10⁻¹⁰
[H⁺] = 6×10⁻⁵

subject: Chemistry
question: Which metal commonly forms an interstitial hydride while retaining its original fcc lattice, among Pd, Cs, Ba, Zn?
explanation: Palladium is the classic example of a metal that absorbs large volumes of hydrogen gas to form an interstitial hydride while largely retaining its original face-centered cubic lattice structure

subject: Chemistry
question: Cesium nitrate and lead nitrate are heated separately. The observation common to both is
options: Brown NO₂ fumes are evolved in both cases
No gas is evolved in either case
Oxygen gas is evolved in both cases
explanation:
Cesium nitrate, like most alkali metal nitrates (except lithium), decomposes on heating to give cesium nitrite and oxygen gas, without brown fumes
Lead nitrate, like other heavy metal nitrates, decomposes to give lead oxide, brown NO₂ fumes, and oxygen gas
While brown fumes are unique to lead nitrate, the evolution of oxygen gas is common to both

subject: Chemistry
question: Identify the incorrect statement regarding compounds of boron
options: Boron trifluoride acts as a Lewis acid
Orthoboric acid is a strong dibasic acid
Borax is used as a flux in metallurgical operations
Diborane reacts with ammonia at low temperature to form an adduct
explanation:
Borax being used as a metallurgical flux, the formation of a BF₃-NH₃ type adduct with ammonia at low temperature, and boron trifluoride behaving as a Lewis acid (due to the electron-deficient boron atom) are all correct facts
However, orthoboric acid (H₃BO₃) is actually a weak monobasic acid, not a strong dibasic acid, since it acts as a Lewis acid accepting a hydroxide ion rather than directly donating more than one proton

subject: Chemistry
question: The number of amphoteric oxides among Ga₂O₃, In₂O₃, Tl₂O₃, Tl₂O is
explanation:
Ga₂O₃, In₂O₃, and Tl₂O₃ are all classified as amphoteric oxides of the group 13 elements
Tl₂O, however, is basic, since the more stable +1 oxidation state of thallium behaves similarly to alkali metal oxides
So the number of amphoteric oxides is 3

subject: Chemistry
question: Which international agreement was signed to phase out substances responsible for ozone layer depletion, such as CFCs?
explanation: The Montreal Protocol, signed in 1987, is the international treaty specifically designed to phase out the production and use of ozone-depleting substances including chlorofluorocarbons

subject: Chemistry
question: A temperature-sensitive organic compound that decomposes near its normal boiling point, and which is immiscible with water, is best purified by
explanation: Steam distillation allows a substance to distill at a temperature well below its normal boiling point using the combined vapor pressure of the substance and steam, avoiding decomposition that would occur under simple distillation

subject: Chemistry
question: Pent-1-ene reacts with water under acid catalysis (Markovnikov addition) to give X. 2-Methylpentane is oxidized at its tertiary carbon to give Y. X and Y respectively are
explanation:
Markovnikov addition of water to pent-1-ene places the hydroxyl group on the more substituted carbon (C2), giving pentan-2-ol as X
Oxidation at the tertiary carbon of 2-methylpentane gives the tertiary alcohol 2-methylpentan-2-ol as Y

subject: Chemistry
question: The IUPAC name of CH₃-CH(CH₃)-CH₂-CH₂-CH₂-OH is
explanation:
Numbering the five-carbon chain to give the hydroxyl group the lowest locant places OH on C1 and the methyl branch on C4
This gives the name 4-methylpentan-1-ol

subject: Chemistry
question: Atoms of element B form a ccp lattice, and atoms of element A occupy half of the octahedral voids and half of the tetrahedral voids. The formula of the compound formed is
explanation:
In a ccp lattice, the effective number of atoms per unit cell is 4, giving 4 octahedral voids and 8 tetrahedral voids
A occupies half of the octahedral voids (2 atoms) and half of the tetrahedral voids (4 atoms), giving 6 atoms of A total
Ratio of A to B = 6:4 = 3:2, so the formula is A₃B₂

subject: Chemistry
question: 4 g of a non-electrolytic, non-volatile solute is dissolved in 50 g of water. The freezing point of the solution is found to be -1.488°Celsius. The molar mass of the solute is (Kf of water = 1.86 K kg/mol)
explanation:
Depression in freezing point = 1.488°Celsius
molality = ¹.⁴⁸⁸⁄₁.₈₆ = 0.8 mol/kg
Moles of solute = 0.8 x 0.05 = 0.04 mol
Molar mass = ⁴⁄₀.₀₄ = 100 g/mol

subject: Chemistry
question: For the cell reaction Fe(s)+Cu²⁺(aq) to Fe²⁺(aq)+Cu(s), given E(Fe²⁺/Fe)=-0.44 V, E(Cu²⁺/Cu)=+0.34 V, and F=96500 C⁄ₘₒₗ, the standard Gibbs free energy change (in kJ/mol) is
explanation:
E(cell) = E(cathode) - E(anode) = 0.34 - (-0.44) = 0.78 V
Number of electrons transferred, n=2
ΔG = -nFE(cell) = -2 x 96500 x 0.78 = -150540 J, which is approximately -150.54 kJ

subject: Chemistry
question: Molten MgCl₂ is electrolyzed. The mass of magnesium produced at the cathode when 2895 amperes is passed for 1500 seconds is (F=96500 C⁄ₘₒₗ, atomic mass of Mg=24)
explanation:
Charge passed, Q = It = 2895 x 1500 = 4342500 C
Equivalents deposited = Q⁄F = ⁴³⁴²⁵⁰⁰⁄₉₆₅₀₀ = 45
Since Mg²⁺ +2e- to Mg, the equivalent weight is ²⁴⁄₂=12
Mass deposited = 45 x 12 = 540 g

subject: Chemistry
question: A reaction rate constant at 700 K is 100 × that at 350 K. Using R=2 cal/K mol and log100=2, the activation energy is approximately
explanation:
Using the Arrhenius equation: 2.303 log(ᵏ²⁄ₖ₁) = (ᴱᵃ⁄R)(¹⁄T₁ - ¹⁄T₂)
2.303(2) = (ᴱᵃ⁄₂)(¹⁄₃₅₀ - ¹⁄₇₀₀)
4.606 = (ᴱᵃ⁄₂)(¹⁄₇₀₀)
4.606 = ᴱᵃ⁄₁₄₀₀
Ea = 6448 cal/mol, which is about 6.45 kcal/mol

subject: Chemistry
question: Which ion is most effective for coagulating a negatively charged starch-iodine sol, among Li⁺, Ca²⁺, Fe³⁺, K⁺?
explanation:
A negatively charged sol requires a cation for coagulation, and by the Hardy-Schulze rule, a higher charge on the ion gives greater coagulating power
Among the given ions, Fe³⁺ has the highest charge and is therefore the most effective coagulant

subject: Chemistry
question: Which of the following are true for chemisorption but NOT for physisorption? I. The rate initially increases with a rise in temperature (up to a point) II. It readily forms multilayers III. It is largely irreversible
explanation:
Chemisorption often shows an initial increase in rate with temperature, since it usually requires overcoming an activation energy barrier, whereas physisorption typically decreases with temperature, so I is a distinguishing feature
Multilayer formation is characteristic of physisorption, not chemisorption, so II is incorrect
Chemisorption is largely irreversible, unlike the readily reversible physisorption, so III is a distinguishing feature
Hence statements I and III are correct

subject: Chemistry
question: Which technique is used to purify low-melting metals like gallium and indium by exploiting differences in melting point through repeated melting-freezing cycles?
explanation: Zone refining exploits the different solubilities of impurities in the molten and solid states of a metal, and is applied to purify various metals, including those with relatively low melting points, using controlled melting-freezing cycles along the length of a rod

subject: Chemistry
question: H₄P₂O₇ (pyrophosphoric acid) is formed when H₃PO₄ is
options: heated strongly, causing two molecules to undergo condensation with loss of water
explanation: When orthophosphoric acid (H₃PO₄) is heated strongly, two molecules undergo a condensation reaction, losing one molecule of water between them, to form pyrophosphoric acid, H₄P₂O₇

subject: Chemistry
question: Regarding SO₃ and the sulfite ion SO₃ 2-, which of the following is correct?
options: SO₃ is pyramidal while SO₃ 2- is trigonal planar
Both have identical hybridization at the central atom
SO₃ is trigonal planar while SO₃ 2- is pyramidal
Both are trigonal planar and identical in shape
explanation:
In the monomeric gas phase, SO₃ has no lone pair on sulfur and adopts a trigonal planar (sp2) shape
The sulfite ion SO₃ 2-, however, has one lone pair on sulfur, giving it a pyramidal (sp3) shape, distinct from SO₃

subject: Chemistry
question: Among Ti, V, Cr, Mn, the element with the highest second ionization enthalpy has a spin-only magnetic moment (in BM) in its +1 oxidation state of
explanation:
Chromium has an anomalously high second ionization enthalpy because Cr⁺ (formed by removing one electron from the ground state configuration 3d5 4s1) has a stable half-filled 3d5 configuration, making removal of a further electron especially difficult
Since Cr⁺ has a d5 configuration with 5 unpaired electrons, its spin-only magnetic moment is √[5×7]=√35, which is approximately 5.92 BM

subject: Chemistry
question: Which of the following is NOT an ambidentate ligand, among CN⁻, NO₂⁻, ethylenediamine (en), SCN-?
explanation:
An ambidentate ligand can bind through either of two chemically different donor atoms
Ethylenediamine is a bidentate ligand with two identical nitrogen donor atoms, not an ambidentate ligand, distinguishing it from CN⁻, NO₂⁻, and SCN-, which are all classic ambidentate ligands

subject: Chemistry
question: Which of the following polymers is classified as a polyamide?
explanation:
Nylon 6 is formed by the ring-opening polymerization of caprolactam and contains repeated amide linkages in its backbone, classifying it as a polyamide
Bakelite is a phenol-formaldehyde resin, while Buna-N and Neoprene are synthetic rubbers (elastomers), none of which are polyamides

subject: Chemistry
question: Match the amino acids Serine, Methionine, Histidine, Proline with their distinguishing features: I. Contains a hydroxyl group in its side chain II. Contains a sulfur atom in its side chain III. Contains an imidazole ring IV. Has a cyclic structure with a secondary amino group
explanation:
Serine has a hydroxyl-containing side chain, matching I
Methionine has a sulfur-containing side chain, matching II
Histidine has an imidazole ring in its side chain, matching III
Proline has a unique cyclic structure with a secondary amino group rather than a primary one, matching IV
So the correct match is A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV, taking A,B,C,D as Serine, Methionine, Histidine, Proline respectively

subject: Chemistry
question: Consider two statements: I. Aspartame is an artificial sweetener that is not suitable for use in cooking at high temperatures II. Broad-spectrum antibiotics are effective against both gram-positive and gram-negative bacteria. The correct option is
options: Statement I is correct but II is not correct
Statement I is not correct but II is correct
Both statements I and II are correct
Both statements I and II are not correct
explanation:
Aspartame is known to break down at high temperatures, losing its sweetness, so it is indeed unsuitable for cooking applications, making statement I correct
Broad-spectrum antibiotics are, by definition, effective against a wide range of both gram-positive and gram-negative bacteria, making statement II also correct

subject: Chemistry
question: A compound C₄H₉Cl reacts faster in a polar protic solvent than in a polar aprotic solvent, and the observed rate law is first order overall with respect to the substrate alone. This behavior is characteristic of a
explanation:
A rate law that is first order in the substrate alone (independent of nucleophile concentration), combined with a preference for polar protic solvents that stabilize the intermediate carbocation, are hallmark features of the SN₁ mechanism
Tertiary halides are well known to favor this SN₁ pathway

subject: Chemistry
question: Pent-1-yne reacts with 2 moles of HBr (Markovnikov addition in both steps). The major product formed is
explanation:
Pent-1-yne undergoes the first Markovnikov addition of HBr, placing bromine on the more substituted carbon (C2) to give 2-bromopent-1-ene
The second addition of HBr, again following Markovnikov orientation with both bromine atoms ending up on the same carbon due to the greater stability of the intermediate carbocation, gives 2,2-dibromopentane as the major product

subject: Chemistry
question: Benzenediazonium chloride reacts with ethanol under mild heating to give
explanation: When a diazonium salt is heated with ethanol, the ethanol acts as a reducing agent (being oxidized to acetaldehyde), and the diazonium group is replaced by hydrogen through reductive deamination, giving benzene

subject: Chemistry
question: The ratio of σ electrons to π electrons in benzonitrile (C₆H₅-C triple bond N) is
explanation:
Benzonitrile has 13 σ bonds: 6 ring C-C, 5 ring C-H (since one ring position is substituted), 1 bond from the ring to the nitrile carbon, and 1 σ bond within the C-triple-bond-N group, giving 26 σ electrons
It has 5 π bonds: 3 from the aromatic ring and 2 from the C-triple-bond-N triple bond, giving 10 π electrons
Ratio of σ electrons to π electrons = 26:10 = 13:5

subject: Chemistry
question: When two equivalents of formaldehyde and one equivalent of an aldehyde lacking an α-hydrogen, such as benzaldehyde, are treated with concentrated NaOH, the Cannizzaro reaction preferentially produces
options: an equal mixture of all four possible products
sodium formate and the corresponding alcohol of the second aldehyde
explanation:
Formaldehyde, being the most reactive and least sterically hindered carbonyl compound, acts as the preferred hydride donor in a crossed Cannizzaro reaction
It is therefore preferentially oxidized to sodium formate, while the other aldehyde (which lacks an α-hydrogen) is preferentially reduced to its corresponding alcohol

subject: Chemistry
question: N,N-Dimethylbenzenesulphonamide, formed by reaction with the Hinsberg reagent, is found to be insoluble in alkali. This indicates it was formed from a reaction with a
explanation:
N,N-Dimethylbenzenesulphonamide has both hydrogen atoms on nitrogen replaced by methyl groups, leaving no N-H bond and thus no acidic hydrogen to react with alkali
This fully N,N-disubstituted product is characteristic of the reaction between the Hinsberg reagent and a secondary amine, such as dimethylamine
